title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 64 (Notice of alteration of share capital)

content.overview: Within 30 days of a share-capital alteration under section 61(1), a qualifying increase under section 62(4) read with section 62(6), or redemption of redeemable preference shares, the company must file the prescribed notice with the Registrar and, where required, the altered memorandum.
content.glance: Within 30 days of a share-capital alteration under section 61(1), a qualifying increase under section 62(4) read with section 62(6), or redemption of redeemable preference shares, the company must file the prescribed notice with the Registrar and, where required, the altered memorandum.
content.study: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 64 (Notice to be given to Registrar for alteration of share capital). The company must file notice in the prescribed form with the Registrar within 30 days where: (a) it alters share capital in a manner specified in section 61(1); (b) a Government order under section 62(4), read with section 62(6), increases the company's authorised capital; or (c) it redeems redeemable preference shares. The filing is accompanied by the altered memorandum where required by the section. Under subsection (2), failure attracts a penalty of ₹500 for each day the default continues, capped at ₹5,00,000 for the company and ₹1,00,000 for an officer in default. Check the prescribed form and any applicable current filing instructions. This is a notice-filing rule, not a general approval procedure for every capital event.

sections.heading: Events that trigger notice
sections.body: Section 64 applies when the company alters share capital in a manner specified in section 61(1), when a Government order under section 62(4) read with section 62(6) increases authorised capital, or when the company redeems redeemable preference shares.

sections.heading: Filing and deadline
sections.body: The company must file notice in the prescribed form with the Registrar within 30 days of the alteration, increase or redemption, along with the altered memorandum as required by the section.

sections.heading: Current penalty
sections.body: For non-compliance with subsection (1), the company and every officer in default are liable to a penalty of ₹500 for each day the default continues, subject to a maximum of ₹5,00,000 for the company and ₹1,00,000 for the officer in default.

examples.body: A company altering share capital under section 61, or increasing members of a company limited by guarantee, must give notice to the Registrar with the altered memorandum.

hypotheticals.question: A company redeems redeemable preference shares. What filing deadline applies under section 64?
hypotheticals.analysis: The company must file the prescribed notice with the Registrar within 30 days of the redemption, along with the altered memorandum as required.

hypotheticals.question: A company fails to file the section 64 notice and the default continues. What is the current penalty cap?
hypotheticals.analysis: The penalty is ₹500 per day while the default continues, capped at ₹5,00,000 for the company and ₹1,00,000 for an officer in default.

distinctions.title: Capital event and notice to Registrar
distinctions.left: Section 61 or a qualifying section 62 order describes the capital event.
distinctions.right: Section 64 imposes a separate notice-filing duty for the specified events, including preference-share redemption.

misconceptions.trap: Treating every capital event as triggering section 64.
misconceptions.correction: Identify one of the specific events listed in section 64(1).

misconceptions.trap: Using the old fine/imprisonment wording or an outdated penalty cap.
misconceptions.correction: Use the amended subsection (2): ₹500 per day, capped at ₹5,00,000 for the company and ₹1,00,000 for an officer in default.

misconceptions.trap: Omitting the 30-day deadline or altered memorandum requirement.
misconceptions.correction: State the prescribed notice, 30-day period and altered memorandum requirement.

questionsAndAnswers.question: Which events trigger section 64?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: A section 61(1) share-capital alteration, a qualifying Government order increasing authorised capital under section 62(4) read with section 62(6), or redemption of redeemable preference shares.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What is the current penalty for failure to file?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: ₹500 per day, capped at ₹5,00,000 for the company and ₹1,00,000 for an officer in default.
